question: A 37-year-old man presents a picture of arthritis of the metacarpophalangeal of both hands and a right pleuritis. On examination, bilateral malar erythema was observed. Positive antinuclear antibodies are detected (titre 1/640), with native anti-DNA antibodies also positive; Anti-Sm negative. What would be the initial treatment of choice for this patient?

options.opd: The picture will probably be self-limiting and does not require treatment.

analysis: The patient presents with symptoms and laboratory findings suggestive of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), including arthritis, pleuritis, malar rash, and positive antinuclear antibodies with native anti-DNA positivity. The initial treatment for SLE, especially with active disease involving arthritis and pleuritis, typically involves glucocorticoids to control inflammation. While non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and antimalarials can be used, they are generally not the first-line treatment in cases with significant systemic involvement. Therefore, high-dose glucocorticoids would be the most appropriate initial treatment.
